newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Bearish East Europe bourses seen extending losses.
newsitem.headline: Bearish East Europe bourses seen extending losses.

text.p: Most central and east European share markets traded lower this week, with a bearish mood hanging over all the major markets apart from Budapest.
Prague and Bratislava were the only markets to post gains but analysts were sceptical these could be sustained, citing currency risk and low liquidity.
The Central European Share Index (CESI), which reflects price movements in 72 Hungarian, Polish, Czech, Slovak and Slovenian stocks, fell by 0.1 percent since last Friday.
PRAGUE

Czech shares staged a brief recovery at the beginning of the week but pessimism, strengthened by instability in the Czech crown, put the PX50 index firmly back on a downward course as the week drew to a close.

"The earlier gains, this was purely speculation. I would say that the periods of the market going up will be very short and the intervals between them longer and longer," said Radek Vavra of Citicorp Securities.
The market was rocked on Thursday by strong downward pressure on the Czech crown which prompted intervention from the central bank and a hike in the repo rate.
BRATISLAVA
Low liquidity continued to characterise trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) this week, with the official SAX index almost unchanged.
"VSZ and partially also Slovnaft have been virtually the only two issues traded, in terms of volumes," Bohus Betko of ING Barings said.
Steel maker VSZ dominated sessions on the bourse floor. It traded 5,445 shares on Thursday alone.
BUDAPEST
Hungarian stocks drifted lower this week as first quarter corporate earnings reports came through from all companies except oil company MOL.
Nevertheless, MOL received the most attention, with a domestic public offering in its shares beginning on Monday. Demand was so high that subscriptions were closed on Wednesday.
Traders said the market generally was, as yet, little moved by the first quarter earnings figures.

But the bourse's overall long-term outlook was said to be positive as corporate earnings, coupled with a recovery in economic activity, were likely to increase the appetite of foreign investors for Hungarian shares.

"We are still very optimistic with the market," said Nigel Rendell, analyst at HSBC James Capel in London. "As far as the foreign investors are concerned, they are looking for the opportunity to buy in Hungary."
WARSAW
The Warsaw WIG index fell with analysts expecting it to be flat next week in the absence of strong fresh factors.
Bank stocks rebounded late in the week, after underperforming the market for the last three months, but analysts saw little upside potential, saying bank earning prospects for 1997 were weak.

They said a drop in year-on-year Polish inflation to 15.3 percent in April, a figure reported on Thursday, was a good sign, but expected only a moderate impact on the market. They said there was no room for a rate cut before June.
In the longer-term the bourse was seen extending its eight-week sideways drift with forthcoming elections and large privatisations cooling demand.
LJUBLJANA
Slovenian shares fell 4.08 percent this week, with the blue-chip SBI index falling 55.36 points to 1,306.32. Turnover fell to 378.6 million tolars from 420.4 million.
Traders said moderate declines were likely to continue as long as foreign buyers stayed away from the Ljubljana bourse.

The central bank in February ordered international portfolio investors to open custody accounts at one of 14 fully licensed Slovenian banks in order to be able to trade in shares. Since then, the index has fallen by over 21 percent, while average daily volume is down by over 75 percent.
ZAGREB
Croatian stocks traded lower on relatively high volumes throughout the week and analysts said the market could fall further in the next month.
The leading issues -- fully listed drugs firm Pliva and Zagrebacka Banka -- continued to slide in line with the performance of their GDRs in London.
BUCHAREST
Two independent indices -- the VAB and the BIG -- fell by 5.5 and 5.93 percent respectively with turnover averaging 7.9 billion lei per session.
Antibiotice pharmaceuticals company was the biggest gainer among top tier stocks, rising 100 lei to close at 5,500, while Oltchim chemical plant was the biggest loser, closing 30 lei weaker at 2,600.
